note: Pattern book: good ideas for demo configuration, from our own deals, competitors' and other vendors' public UX and documentation, the Knowledge Hub and anything an SC spots. Ideas, not rules: sc-demo-plan suggests them, the SC chooses. Screenshots live in SharePoint Patterns/<id>/. New patterns arrive through SharePoint Patterns/_inbox (sc-inbox).
fields: id, name, what, why_it_works, pains (in plain words), build (native | custom | ai), how (in Creatio), effort_h, differentiators, ai_part, source, proven (deal + date) or idea, shots

patterns.name: Whole job on one board
patterns.what: One screen per project or site with a column per stage, cards for what to sell at each stage, and won / still to win / lost at the top.
patterns.why_it_works: The customer sees their whole job the way they think about it, not as a list of records.
pains: projects get lost inside the customer account
reps can't see what's left to win
patterns.how: Custom Freedom UI component (usr.HgBuildBoard, JS only, no compile) as the first tab of the site page; status menu on each card.
patterns.ai_part: AI flags items past their stage with nothing quoted.

patterns.name: Templates the business owns
patterns.what: Pick a type (job type, product, case type) and the record fills itself from a template the business edits: stages, lines, checklists.
patterns.why_it_works: Shows the business changing the system the same day, which is the live change.
pains: new products take months to set up
patterns.how: Template object + lines, a business process on create copies the lines; template builder page (H&G used a custom builder, a native list works).
patterns.ai_part: AI proposes template lines from a description.

patterns.name: Gaps that become coaching
patterns.what: A home page that shows, per site and per rep, what was identified on time, late or never, so missed work becomes a coaching list.
patterns.why_it_works: Turns data into a manager's conversation; managers buy this.
pains: we don't know what we missed
patterns.how: Custom home (usr.HgSalesOverview) with a site-by-stage map and rep scorecards; a native dashboard with a chart by rep is the light version.
patterns.ai_part: Weekly AI summary of each rep's gaps for the manager.

patterns.name: Rules as data
patterns.what: A small table the business owns (priorities, thresholds, steps per channel) that processes and AI read, so behaviour changes without touching a process.
patterns.why_it_works: The safest, fastest live change: edit a row, see the system behave differently.
patterns.how: One rules object per stand (labPackRule pattern, M6 kit §3); processes and AI skills read it.
patterns.ai_part: The AI agent reads the table, so its answer changes too.

patterns.name: My day home page
patterns.what: A role's home page: their numbers first, today's work planned by the system, and which items are ready.
patterns.why_it_works: Opens the demo on their outcome (demo bar item 2).
patterns.how: Freedom UI home page: KPI tiles, today's list, a status column; see creatio-dashboards-homepages.
patterns.ai_part: A 'today' summary from the AI Twin.

patterns.name: Customer 360 with 'what to raise next'
patterns.what: One page per customer or outlet: open issues, orders, what's on the shelf, who decides, and what to raise next time.
patterns.why_it_works: The rep's question is 'what do I need to know before I walk in'; this answers it on one screen.
patterns.how: Custom Angular page (outlet360-ws) for the full version; native record page with tabs and a summary strip for the light version.
patterns.ai_part: The 'what to raise' list comes from the briefing agent (P07).

patterns.name: Agent drafts, person confirms
patterns.what: An AI agent prepares something useful (a briefing, a summary, a reply), ranks it by business rules, and saves only when the user confirms; every confirmation is logged.
patterns.why_it_works: Shows AI doing real work and shows control: the two things buyers worry about.
pains: worried about AI acting on its own
patterns.how: Creatio.ai skill on the record or AI Studio agent; confirm-then-act through an action process; a log object (see creatio-ai-skill-prompts).

patterns.name: Read it to me on the drive
patterns.what: The same briefing as audio, so a field user hears it on the way to the visit.
patterns.why_it_works: Memorable, and fits how field people actually work.
pains: reps don't open the app before a visit
patterns.how: Text-to-speech of the briefing (recorded clip for the demo, voice agent later).

patterns.name: Steps that follow the channel
patterns.what: The same visit or case runs different steps depending on its type (licensed vs not, direct vs partner), set by a rule.
patterns.why_it_works: Proves one platform handles different ways of working without separate apps.
pains: the tool was built for one way of selling
patterns.how: Visit or case steps driven by a rules row (P04); mobile page with required steps.
patterns.ai_part: AI fills the visit record from what the rep says at check-out.

patterns.name: Stage bar on the record
patterns.what: A stage progress bar (DCM) on the main record, so the record shows where the job is up to.
patterns.why_it_works: Familiar, clear, and moving it is a natural live moment.
pains: no one knows where a job is up to
patterns.how: Case (DCM) on the object + a page template with a progress bar.
patterns.ai_part: AI suggests moving the stage when a note says the job has moved on.

patterns.name: Quick-add with automatic assignment
patterns.what: A short form to capture an enquiry fast, then a process assigns it to the right person and creates their first task.
patterns.why_it_works: Shows speed to first response in under a minute.
patterns.how: Quick-add mini page + assignment process + task.
patterns.ai_part: AI reads the enquiry email and fills the form.

patterns.name: AI step in the background
patterns.what: A process step where AI reads something that arrives (email, document, note), extracts or classifies it and fills the record, with no click from the user; a person reviews exceptions.
patterns.why_it_works: Shows AI doing work nobody wants to do, inside a normal process (demo bar item 5).
pains: manual data entry from emails or documents
patterns.how: Business process with an AI step (Creatio.ai) on receipt; review queue for low confidence.
patterns.proven: not built yet (idea; first planned for the PRC referral proof, Nov 2026)

patterns.name: Explainer line and KPI strip on list pages
patterns.what: Every key list page gets one plain sentence saying what it's for and a small strip of the numbers that matter.
patterns.why_it_works: Cheap, and it makes a standard list look designed for them (demo bar item 6).
patterns.how: Freedom UI label + indicator widgets above the list; hide noise columns.

patterns.name: Portal for the other side
patterns.what: A portal for customers, partners or employees on the same data, with their own view and actions.
patterns.why_it_works: Shows one platform reaching people outside the CRM users.
pains: customers or partners email and call for status
patterns.how: Freedom UI portal, or custom Angular portal for a richer experience (Scentia).
patterns.ai_part: A portal agent answers status questions from the records.

patterns.name: Document beside its extracted fields
patterns.what: A review screen with the incoming document on one side and the fields AI read from it on the other, unsure fields highlighted, one click to confirm or correct.
patterns.why_it_works: People trust AI reading when they can see the source next to the result, and the confirm step gets fast.
patterns.how: Native record page with the file preview and the extracted fields side by side; a custom side-by-side viewer is the richer option (+4 h).
patterns.ai_part: Pairs with P12 (the background AI step).
patterns.source: outside: Google Document AI human review documentation (read 11 Nov 2026), via the PRC plan

patterns.name: Proof scoreboard
patterns.what: A page that tracks a proof against its success criteria: items processed, accuracy against the right answers, time saved, exceptions, updated as the proof runs.
patterns.why_it_works: The readout is about their numbers, not our demo, and it feeds the business case.
pains: we need evidence before we decide
patterns.how: A proof-results object plus a dashboard with one indicator per success criterion.
patterns.ai_part: AI summary of the week's results for the readout.
